title: Russian attacks on Ukrainian civilians may have a domestic dimension
gist: The article argues Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilians surged 59 percent in 2026 and, beyond military and diplomatic logic, serve a domestic propaganda purpose of projecting military progress amid stalemate and Ukrainian strikes inside Russia; escalation is expected to continue.

insights.claim: UN data show 2,570 Ukrainian civilians killed and 15,211 injured in the first nine months of 2026, a 59 percent increase on the previous year.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Civilian toll is rising sharply, pointing to intensifying air campaign and growing infrastructure damage.
insights.locator: Russian attacks on the Ukrainian civilian population have escalated

insights.claim: Russian missile and drone strikes force Ukrainian businesses to shutter, stop ports from operating and close entire industrial plants.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Economic damage in Ukraine extends beyond casualties, affecting ports and industry.

insights.claim: With front lines barely moving in 2026 and Russian gains tiny, attacks on civilian infrastructure may look like the most realistic way to break Ukrainian resistance.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Stalemate on the ground raises the likelihood of continued strikes on energy and civilian targets.

insights.claim: Ukraine has offered concessions including accepting current front lines as a settlement basis but refuses to cede land Moscow could not seize, so the Kremlin may use civilian strikes to raise diplomatic pressure.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Strikes may be coercive bargaining; expect pressure to intensify around negotiations.
insights.locator: The diplomatic situation is similarly stalemated

insights.claim: The strategy is costly for Russia, which is depleting its own missile and drone stockpiles without changing the territorial balance or forcing capitulation.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Stockpile depletion is a constraint to watch on the sustainability of the campaign.
insights.locator: However, this strategy is not without costs

insights.claim: Bombing Ukrainian civilians may let Russia create the illusion of military progress for a domestic audience that expected quick victory and instead faces a war of attrition.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Domestic political needs may make the campaign hard to de-escalate even if militarily ineffective.
insights.locator: Why, then, does Moscow continue to expand

insights.claim: Russian war bloggers describe target selection as a mystery, suggesting decisions follow the principle of hitting something.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Suggests strikes lack clear military targeting logic.

insights.claim: In August the Russian Defense Ministry's Telegram channel celebrated bombardment of Ukrainian cities, and a post mockingly promising to freeze the war over winter drew over 650,000 views and tens of thousands of approving responses.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Indicates public endorsement of targeting civilian heating and power networks ahead of winter.
insights.quote: “there are enough missiles and drones for everyone.”
insights.locator: Government accounts also play an important role

insights.claim: Ukrainian drones reaching Moscow and St. Petersburg and fuel shortages across Russia are undermining the Kremlin's success narrative, increasing the value to it of visible strikes on Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Ukrainian deep strikes and fuel shortages are pressure points on Russian domestic sentiment.
insights.locator: This has become even more important over the past year

insights.claim: Russia is likely to keep escalating attacks on Ukraine's population and infrastructure, which will make cities less livable but are unlikely to prove militarily decisive.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Expect continued winter-season energy infrastructure targeting; plan for sustained Ukrainian grid risk.
